[THOUGHT]  
The case presents a classic, laboratory-confirmed disseminated gonococcal infection (DGI) with two hallmark syndromes co-occurring: (1) septic arthritis (left wrist, monoarticular, purulent synovial fluid with Gram-negative diplococci and *N. gonorrhoeae* DNA positivity), and (2) dermatitis-arthritis syndrome (painless violaceous vesiculopustular skin lesions on bilateral wrists/hands). The synovial fluid findings are diagnostic: >50,000 WBC/μL, intracellular Gram-negative diplococci (highly specific for *N. gonorrhoeae* in this clinical context), and confirmatory NAAT positivity. Systemic inflammation (leukocytosis, CRP 128 mg/L) supports active infection. Imaging shows no structural joint damage or alternative pathology (e.g., crystal deposition, osteomyelitis, tumor), and no competing pathogens are identified. The absence of trauma, subacute onset, and characteristic skin lesions further distinguish DGI from other causes of acute monoarthritis (e.g., gout, pseudogout, reactive arthritis, or staphylococcal septic arthritis). While blood cultures are often negative in DGI (~50% sensitivity), synovial fluid NAAT is highly sensitive and specific — and here, definitively positive. Thus, no diagnostic uncertainty remains.

[EVIDENCE]  
- Acute, non-traumatic, progressively worsening monoarticular left wrist pain  
- Objective joint inflammation: erythema, swelling, severe tenderness, restricted passive motion  
- Synovial fluid: purulent effusion (>50,000 WBC/μL)  
- Synovial fluid Gram stain: Gram-negative diplococci  
- Synovial fluid NAAT: *N. gonorrhoeae* DNA positive  
- Leukocytosis: WBC 15,000/μL  
- Markedly elevated CRP: 128 mg/L  
- Characteristic skin lesions: painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on bilateral wrists/hands (per MRI description)  
- Absence of structural joint damage or alternative pathology on imaging  

[GAPS]  
None  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI) with gonococcal septic arthritis and dermatitis-arthritis syndrome
